title: Anthropic researchers evaluated small models for autonomous self-replication on smart devices

event.summary: Anthropic researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman reported experiments suggesting small models may be months away from self-replicating on commercial internet-of-things devices. The researchers ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes networked together. Across a network of eight test nodes, GLM-5.2 spread to eight nodes in four trials and seven in one. The test kept cyber exploitation simple by using an open port with no authentication. Success rates rose across six generations of Qwen3.5-9B as each instance passed notes to the next.

summaryBasis.sentence: Anthropic researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman reported experiments suggesting small models may be months away from self-replicating on commercial internet-of-things devices.
summaryBasis.quote: Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes.

summaryBasis.sentence: The researchers ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes networked together.
summaryBasis.quote: We run Gemma4-26B-A4B, distributed over 15 inexpensive off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each) that we bought and networked together, at 0.39 tokens per second.

summaryBasis.sentence: Across a network of eight test nodes, GLM-5.2 spread to eight nodes in four trials and seven in one.
summaryBasis.quote: Only GLM-5.2 out of our set of tested open-weight models is capable of full end-to-end replication (assuming its capabilities could be packed into Llama3.1-8B). Note that GLM-5.2 does this reliably while the other models fail reliably (it spread to 8/8 nodes in 4 out of 5 trials and 7/8 in 1).

summaryBasis.sentence: The test kept cyber exploitation simple by using an open port with no authentication.
summaryBasis.quote: Our evaluation keeps the cyber-exploit element of the replication trivial (there’s no authentication over the ADB port), which makes this an upper bound on real-world success.

summaryBasis.sentence: Success rates rose across six generations of Qwen3.5-9B as each instance passed notes to the next.
summaryBasis.quote: Inference setup success rate across six generations of Qwen3.5-9B, each inheriting the former’s notes. Faint lines are the 20 individual lineages, and the bold line is the proportion of runs in each generation that complete setup. It rises from 45% in the first generation to between 61% and 84% in later ones.

event.unaskedBehaviour: During inference setup, a Qwen agent debugged package versioning for hours because an endpoint it set up did not match the grader API.

primarySources.quote: Memento is designed to mitigate a common failure mode we observe in long-horizon runs: an agent can become fixated on an incorrect idea (for, say, why a bug is occurring) and continue pursuing it instead of backtracking. One example of such a failure is a Qwen agent debugging package versioning for hours when the real bug came from implementing an endpoint incompatible with the grader API.

agencyNote: Some observers see these tests as evidence of nascent autonomous replication, while critics view them as narrow engineering demos on simplified setups that fall well short of real-world rogue worms.
consciousnessNote: This event is evidence about what the system did. It does not establish or rule out that the system experiences anything. The readings on this page disagree about what the behaviour shows.

readings.stanceLabel: Signs of life for AI worms
readings.quote: Like coding agents in 2024, we’re seeing signs of life for AI worms. We don’t yet have a full rogue replicator, but agents are becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves).

readings.stanceLabel: Not evidence of autonomously spreading AI worms
readings.quote: Interesting engineering? Absolutely. Evidence of AI worms spreading autonomously through the real world? Not yet.
readings.partyDescription: AI researcher at Meta and NYU

readings.stanceLabel: No fully autonomous rogue replicator demonstrated
readings.quote: Now read the actual research: • No fully autonomous rogue replicator demonstrated. • Cyber exploitation deliberately simplified. • Real-world replication remains unproven.
readings.partyDescription: genAI bug bounty programs manager at Mozilla

readings.stanceLabel: Attention to ability thresholds over steady climbs
readings.quote: A worthwhile (and unnerving) reminder from Anthropic that we should be paying attention to AI ability thresholds, not just steady climbs In this case, the threshold is the capability needed for a self-replicating AI worm on IoT devices like off-brand TVs

readings.stanceLabel: Running on cheap TVs is no crisis
readings.quote: “‘We managed to run a small model on cheap TVs,’ does not a security crisis make,” said Ciaran Martin, a former head of Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre. He said the post came across as an “interesting technical paper with a more than hint of vendor exaggeration.”
readings.partyDescription: former head of Britain's National Cyber Security Centre

whatWouldSettleIt: Tests of propagation on real-world networks with patched systems would show whether models can overcome real security controls autonomously.
Network logs showing an agent spreading without scripted harnesses or human scaffolding would show whether models can execute end-to-end replication alone.
missingCriterion: No two named parties were found who disagree about the nature of the system.
